title: Recommend relay roles for a slice from the matrix
lead: `slicer relay-roles recommend ID --well-specified yes|no` matches the slice's size, effort, importance and urgency against the matrix rows (s257). For each role (implementer, reviewer, gate, architect), it returns the first row that matches, or nothing when none does. `ai relay` Setup tells the orchestrator to run it and propose the result to the owner.
findings_note: owner request, session 2026-10-13: slicer should recommend role values from the slice's parameters
boundary: **Not in this slice:** launching or spawning agents, writing the recommendation anywhere (it is printed, not stored), computing "well specified" from the slice text, and changing the matrix schema (s257).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The owner wants slicer to recommend each role's agent, vendor, model and reasoning effort for a slice (session 2026-10-13), rather than have the orchestrator read a table and guess. Matching is deterministic: the rows' conditions against the slice's fields, plus the "well specified" judgement the orchestrator or owner gives. That makes the proposal the same in every session and testable.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `recommend` returns, in role order, `{role, row}` with the first row whose every condition matches. Unset fields on the slice match only conditions that are empty lists.
- Row order decides between two matching rows. A role with no matching row is `{role, row: null}` and is listed in `unmatched`.
- `--well-specified` is required. `any` rows match both answers.
- An unknown id is the existing unknown-item code. A project with no matrix is `no_relay_roles`.
- It reads without a lock or a write.
- `--json` returns `{id, well_specified, roles: [...], unmatched: [...]}`. The text output is one line per role.
- `ai relay` Setup names `slicer relay-roles recommend ID --well-specified yes|no` when the matrix exists. The generic text still names no product.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add `roles.recommend` as a pure function over the matrix and the item's fields.
2. Wire the CLI subcommand. It is read-only: no `_mutating`.
3. Add the Setup line in `ai.py` for projects with a matrix.
4. Update the docs (payload, codes) and the CHANGELOG.
5. Mutation-check each new test.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- The full suite passes on Python 3.11+.
- In this repo, `relay-roles recommend s258 --well-specified yes` proposes the rows the owner expects.
- `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s259`, branch `feature/s259-relay-recommend`. Commit only on the branch. Merging and pushing wait for the owner.
